title: Writing, Appending and File Modes
learningObjectives: Explain the main rules of file writing modes.
Identify the key C++ constructs used for file writing modes.
Apply file writing modes in a small program.
Recognize common failure cases and safety concerns.
Test a practical scenario and justify the chosen approach.

understand.concept: ofstream opens files for output. out generally truncates existing content; app preserves existing contents and directs each write to the end; ate only sets the initial file position. Use flags combined with |.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the wrong mode can destroy earlier data or write in the wrong place.

practise.guidedTask: Create a file with a heading, append three entries, then intentionally truncate it. Compare before/after and explain each mode.
practise.independentTask: Build a small logger with append and replace modes. Validate opening, writing and flushing; test against an existing file.
